content: The recommended dosage for Cetraria islandica (commonly known as Iceland moss) is 4 to 6 grams per day, divided into three doses, taken orally. Alternatively, 5 to 3 grams of the dried plant can be steeped in 150 mL of boiling water for 5 to 10 minutes, then strained, and consumed as a tea several times daily. This plant is traditionally used for conditions such as bronchitis, cough, fever, dyspepsia, loss of appetite, sore throat, and vomiting. It exhibits anti-inflammatory, antiemetic, and demulcent properties. Additionally, it has been reported to act as a galactagogue, promoting milk production. At routine doses, no adverse effects have been identified. However, excessive doses or prolonged use may lead to gastrointestinal irritation and liver problems. In rare cases, external application of the plant may cause sensitivity reactions. Regarding pregnancy, Iceland moss is classified as Pregnancy Category A, meaning it is generally considered safe. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Similarly, no adverse effects have been reported during lactation.
